claims: n297/n297_witness.yaml states 297 unit squares, centre and basis (cos, sin) as exact rationals, in a square of exact rational side, as a packing.squares:Witness/v2 document with the softschema envelope and a claim block; the root README and n297/README.md round the side up at 12 places as 17.739455558289, and n297/README.md cuts it at 50 places, 17.73945555828895172457454811760973557490907042860652. n297/n297_exact.json states the same packing as [center_x, center_y, cos, sin] rows with the side.

n297/README.md says the packing keeps the layout of the Squares Project record T-174 (packing by Francisco Couzo, exact optimum by Evan Daniel, refinement by PingYou Ltd): an upper left and a lower right block of axis-aligned squares with staircase edges, a block of 10 squares in the lower left and in the upper right corner, and a diagonal band of 18 columns of tilted squares. It says two things are new: each staircase has two steps of double size, at the 6th and 13th band columns, between which the band lies one staircase step closer to the upper left block, the upper left block holding 6 squares fewer and the lower right block 4 more, the column at each double step holding 7 squares and the other 16 columns 6, so the band holds 110 squares and the blocks 187; and the band columns lean in two groups, by 0.375 degrees one way on the lower left and the other way on the upper right (89 of the 110 band squares), where the record's columns lean in four groups by 0.260 degrees, so one change of lean direction remains where the record has three. It says the double step was taken from the staircases of its n = 132 and n = 157 pinwheels.

n297/README.md says the band was optimized by a sequence of linear programs, restarted many times from random changes to groups of band squares; two series of restarts with different seeds ended at 17.7394555582889; a linear program over all 297 squares found no first-order improvement; the 4289 contact equations of the result were solved in 330-digit arithmetic and hold to 1e-306, the 33 other near contacts staying open by at least 2.1e-7; and the certificate's side is 1.8e-59 above that solution. It says the place where the lean changes was tried one and two columns either side of the middle, before the restarts, at 17.7394733018 for the middle and 17.7394781380 for the others; that the local optimum statement has no formal proof; and that the Kaggle competition 'Squares in Squares' per-puzzle leaderboard listed 17.7404101723 as the best side for n = 297 on 13 November 2026 and shows no packings.

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (area of the clipped intersection of each close pair), both Python's fractions.Fraction and standard library only, are the folder's two exact checkers; #977 says they share one author, Fraction and the input file but no code, report 297 squares and 632 close pairs, and that the witness validates against this repository's witness.schema.yaml at 7629f5a. n297_solution_250_digits.txt gives the side and each square's x, y and angle in radians. The README says the construction, optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificate, checking and figures were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under the direction of Joost de Winter. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
